highlights.title: The M5 MacBook Air just got its biggest discount since Apple raised the price
highlights.summary: If you’ve been holding off on buying a new MacBook Air since Apple raised prices by $200 in June, you’re in luck. The 13-inch M5 MacBook Air is on sale at Amazon and Best Buy with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage starting at $999 ($300 off) for Black Friday, which is the lowest price we’ve seen…
body: The M5-equipped MacBook Air is a good middle ground if you need more power than the MacBook Neo — which, thanks to a $100 discount, is $599 — but don’t want to splurge on a MacBook Pro. Its faster chip, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage make it better suited for multitasking and creative work in apps like Photoshop and Premiere. You also get a higher-resolution display, better speakers, a backlit keyboard that makes typing in the dark easier, and faster ports. Plus, its sharper webcam supports Apple’s Center Stage feature, which automatically adjusts the framing to keep you in view during video calls.

Of course, the Air can’t match the performance or higher-end displays you can get with a MacBook Pro, whether you opt for an M5 model, the newer M5 Pro model with a PROLED XDR Display, or one of the M6-powered machines. A Pro may be worth the extra money if you regularly edit video or work on more demanding creative projects. But if you mostly need a laptop for work, browsing, and occasional photo or video editing, the M5 Air is more than capable.

highlights.summary: Xabi Alonso called for his Chelsea side to get back to the fundamentals before kick-off - and then watched on as they were outworked and outclassed on their way to a miserable 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest.
body: "Everyone in the club and team, we need to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it and we are responsible," Alonso told Sky Sports after the game, which marked their third successive defeat in the Premier League.
"It is a difficult moment for everyone at the club. For the team and the fans. Disappointed to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions.
"We can't stop. We are low in confidence. At this level you need to hold results and not concede so much. That is why we are losing."

highlights.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
highlights.summary: Aside from dealing with my calendar, there's one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I'm about to miss the bus. What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house.
body: You can have a good time brewing up widgets — as long as you don’t expect too much.

Google announced the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous.

I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that shows a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one big pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did.

highlights.title: 7 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics About Food
highlights.summary: Anything can be the star of a Far Side comic. While most of them featured stupid humans or talking animals as their main characters, the surrealist streak in cartoonist Gary Larson sometimes gave life to inanimate objects as well.
body: Here are the seven funniest Far Side comics that star food, some of which feature food that has even gained sentience for the sake of a perfect joke.

I love this comic strip because it is just unabashedly silly. Not only are sandwiches alive in this one-panel reality, but they have such a complex social structure that they even have their own organized crime. The sandwich mafia is so cruel that it punishes its victims by hurling them into a pit of fourth-graders. If I were the sandwich, I’d be especially worried about the fourth-grader in the green stripey shirt. He looks vicious.
Yet another food item that has turned to a life of crime. Here, Larson interprets potato salad going bad in the silliest way possible​​​​​​​.

This is a twist on that classic gag where, with two people in a life boat, one begins to imagine the other as food. This one features​​​​​​​ a man and a cow in a lifeboat​​​​​​​, so the man naturally imagines steak while looking at the cow​​​​​​​. As for the cow, well, he dreams of the man as a pile of man-shaped grass.

highlights.title: Indonesian Cinema’s Next Chapter Is Reaching the World ‘Without Losing Our Cultural Identity,’ Says JAFF Market Director Linda Gozali
highlights.summary: Indonesia’s film industry has momentum at home. JAFF Market director Linda Gozali wants to help it travel. Gozali runs the industry market attached to the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF), now in its third edition.
body: “Our next chapter is learning how to reach international audiences without losing our cultural identity,” Gozali tells Variety. “We aspire to become nationally indispensable, regionally relevant and internationally connected.”

Local hits have yet to translate into comparable business abroad, which Gozali puts down to producers and filmmakers treating the home market as their first priority. “Indonesia has learned how to win its own audiences,” she says, adding that plenty of untapped local viewers still need to be brought in.

Even so, Gozali says, a good share of Indonesian horror has sold across multiple territories, and independent films have been well received on the international festival circuit. She also notes that Indonesia is not alone in looking inward first, pointing to other populous countries such as China, India and Japan.
“Any growth should not be mistaken for maturity,” she says. “JAFF Market’s responsibility is to transform that growth into sustainability.”

highlights.title: Anh Do: ‘When your mum believes in you, you’ve got no option but to make sure you succeed’
highlights.summary: The standup comedian, writer and artist on what made him stop doing art, and the tragedy that prompted him to pick up a paintbrush again. Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads. Most Tafe students are fresh out of high school.
body: “This 18-year-old bloke comes up to me and goes, ‘Geez, you look like Anh Do.’ I said, ‘Yeah, that’s because I am.’ And he goes, ‘Nah, you’re not, but you bloody look like him,’ and walks off,” Do says. He eventually convinced the teenager that he was, in fact, the real Anh Do – and a friendship was born. “I’m still mates with him now!”

I believe him – within a few minutes of meeting Do, now 49, it’s clear he is one of those people with the preternatural ability to befriend anyone. Standing at our meeting spot outside a large converted warehouse in the Sydney suburb of Newtown, Do spots me first – he cartoonishly swivels around, erupts with an oversized wave and tells me how excited he is for our chat. He then launches into jovial, mile-a-minute conversation before I can even clip his mic on. Do is full of anecdotes like his Tafe run-in – some of which are written on the palm of his hand, so he doesn’t forget to bring them up (“I’m just going to give you my best stories, and you put in whatever you want to!”).

highlights.title: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
highlights.summary: German company Q.ANT is trying to cut the amount of energy required to run AI models by using light to perform the toughest calculations.
body: As artificial intelligence becomes an unavoidable part of everyday life and models become ever more sophisticated, the cost of the energy required to run the technology is ballooning.

To rein in runaway costs, AI labs and cloud providers are trying to build new data centers in places with cheap and plentiful renewable energy— like Scandinavia. But logistical challenges, a scarcity of key components, and a swell of anti-data center protests are getting in the way.

An expanding field of hardware startups, among them German company Q.ANT, is coming at the problem from a different direction: by developing a new breed of chip— photonic processors —meant to minimize the amount of energy that AI models consume.

Whereas regular GPUs transmit and process data by shuffling electrons around, photonic processors use waves of light. Because light doesn’t generate heat as it travels and allows more data to be processed simultaneously, photonic processors supposedly consume less energy and require minimal cooling—one of the largest sources of cost for data centers.

highlights.title: No Rodgers, no problem! Steelers shock Broncos after dramatic week
highlights.summary: It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.
body: Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.

Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.

TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.
The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.

highlights.title: Southeast Asian Cinema’s Global Rise Needs Long-Term Backing to Last, Says JAFF Chief Ifa Isfansyah
highlights.summary: The quality and international profile of Southeast Asian cinema have grown sharply, and Ifa Isfansyah, festival director of Indonesia’s Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF), wants countries to build on that by treating film as part of their cultural strategy.
body: He singles out the Philippines for its consistency in developing talent and keeping a presence abroad.

Isfansyah is also one of Indonesia’s leading independent producers. He founded Forka Films, formerly Fourcolours Films, in 2001, and his producing credits include Kamila Andini’s “Yuni” and “Before, Now & Then,” as well as her latest, “Four Seasons in Java,” which played Toronto’s Centerpiece program and Busan this year.

“I believe countries need to recognize cinema as an important part of their cultural strategy, not merely as an industry or a source of national prestige,” he says. “This requires long-term investment, institutional support, and a commitment to building sustainable connections with the international film community.”

JAFF’s 21st edition drew more than 1,000 submissions, from which the festival picked 254 films from 34 countries. The program runs under the theme “Influx,” opening with Lawrence Fajardo’s Filipino drama “Silenced Nights” and closing with Ueda Makoto’s Japanese comedy-drama “You Are the Film.”

highlights.summary: On Friday, No. 3 Texas had its defense lead the way to a 16-6 win at Texas A&M. With the victory, Texas (10-2, 7-2) advances to play Georgia in next weekend's SEC Championship Game in Atlanta.
body: COLLEGE STATION – After surviving an evening on Texas A&M's campus, the Texas football team is heading to Atlanta.

On Friday, No. 3 Texas had its defense lead the way to a 16-6 win over Texas A&M at Kyle Field. With its fourth straight win in this in-state rivaly, Texas (10-2, 7-2) advances to play Georgia in next weekend's SEC Championship Game at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

The Longhorns got some offense in Friday's victory as Cam Coleman hauled in a touchdown and Gianni Spetic kicked three field goals. Texas A&M (4-8) finishes its third season under head coach Mike Elko with its fewest wins since 2008. The Aggies were just 1-8 in SEC play.

highlights.title: France Knights ‘Autobiography,’ ‘Tiger Stripes’ Producer Yulia Evina Bhara at JAFF Market
highlights.summary: Indonesian producer Yulia Evina Bhara, whose credits include Venice title “Autobiography” and Cannes Critics’ Week winner “Tiger Stripes,” was named a Chevalier dans l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres at a ceremony at JAFF Market in Yogyakarta.
body: France created the order in 1957, and its cinema honorees range from Agnès Varda, François Truffaut, Martin Scorsese and Isabelle Huppert to Indonesia’s Garin Nugroho. Filmmaker Joko Anwar received it last year.

“When I read the names of the people who received this before me, I felt very small,” Bhara said. “They are writers, painters, musicians, directors, and many of them are my heroes. So when the letter came, my first thought was, maybe this is a mistake. My second was, this is not only for me, and this is true. A film producer never works alone. A producer is like a person who builds a boat, but the boat only moves when people row together.”

In his address, Penone traced Bhara’s path from Way Kanan in Sumatra’s Lampung province through seven years of producing historical theater, a craft she taught herself, before she turned to film in 2012 with a foundation that used art to revisit the past. She set up KawanKawan Media in Jakarta in 2016, with international co-production at the core of the business from day one. The company’s name is Indonesian for “friends.”

highlights.title: 63 Years Later, CBS's Legendary 70-Episode Series Still Has the Only Vampire Worth Watching
highlights.summary: It’s Fangsgiving here at Polygon, our Thanksgiving celebration of stories about fanged creatures of all types and especially vampires. I didn't want to be left out, but, to be honest, I always thought vampires were kind of dumb. They're a horror movie staple, but they’re rarely all that scary.
body: The only vampire character I ever really had any affection for is Grandpa Munster from the 1964 black-and-white sitcom The Munsters.

The Munsters debuted in 1964 and lasted for just two seasons, but in that time they produced a whopping 70 episodes. The show is about a family of monsters living a normal life in the suburbs and freaking out nearly everyone they encounter. The head of the family is Herman Munster (Fred Gwynne), who is Frankenstein’s monster. He is married to a vampire named Lily (Yvonne De Carlo), and they have​​​​​​​ a werewolf son named Eddie (Butch Patrick). Also living with them is their entirely normal, non-monster niece, Marilyn (Beverley Owen/Pat Priest). And best of all is Grandpa Munster, a several-hundred-year-old vampire​​​​​​​ played by Al Lewis.

To be clear, Grandpa is a pretty crappy vampire. A running gag on the show is his trying (and failing) to bite people. He also can go out during the day and casts a reflection without issue. So, really, he’s a vampire in name only, which might scare off some vampire purists. But if you’re interested in checking out some great Grandpa-centric episodes of The Munsters, here are five of the best.

highlights.title: Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5
highlights.summary: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
body: Thanks to our partnership with AWS, we were lucky enough to get access to a Trainium3 machine ( trn3.48xlarge, 64 NeuronCores) for a month. We spent most of the month testing Hugging Face models on it, and getting more of them to work.
With five days left, I allowed myself a little fun. When you have a Ferrari, every now and then you want to take it out on the track. So I asked myself: what if I tried to generate videos?

I picked LTX-2.5 from Lightricks, which generates video and sound together. By the end, once the models were loaded, a 10-second clip with sound took 22 to 23 s to generate, on half of the machine. Here is the result.

I had two goals. The first was to see how easy it is to generate videos with diffusers on Trainium3. Not the simple clips from the examples: I wanted to make short films from a script, closer to a real use case, like drafting a movie. The second was performance. I wanted to get close to what you get with CUDA, or with LTX's own API.
